skill.name: literature-review
skill.description: Conduct systematic literature reviews across biomedical, scientific, and technical sources. The skill guides search planning, screening, synthesis, citation verification, and markdown or PDF output.
skill.summary: Create systematic literature reviews with documented searches, verified citations, and formatted outputs.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, documentation links, literature-search terminology, or a bracket heuristic on readable Python. Confirmed risks are bounded to Pandoc execution on user-supplied files, output-file writes, and intended DOI/CrossRef network calls. No prompt-injection override was found, but the skill contains low-severity behavioral concerns around mandatory cross-skill image generation and hosted-platform promotion.

remediation.issue: Pandoc conversion runs external local tools on user-selected files.
remediation.suggestion: Document this trust boundary, avoid converting untrusted markdown, restrict input and output paths, and run PDF generation in a sandbox when possible.

remediation.issue: Citation verification sends DOI values to DOI.org and CrossRef.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the outbound requests, ask before network use in privacy-sensitive reviews, and keep timeouts and rate limiting enabled.

remediation.issue: Result and citation scripts write files based on user-provided or derived paths.
remediation.suggestion: Refuse unsafe absolute paths, warn before overwriting existing files, and prefer writing into an explicit review workspace.

remediation.issue: The skill includes mandatory cross-skill image generation and hosted-platform promotion.
remediation.suggestion: Make figure generation optional, require user confirmation for extra tool use, and remove promotional instructions from the operational workflow.

semantic_findings.title: Mandatory Cross-Skill Image Generation
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md instructs that every literature review must include AI-generated figures using another skill. This can cause unnecessary external tool use and should be optional or user-confirmed.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction is explicit and located in the main skill workflow. It affects behavior but does not show secret access, exfiltration, or command injection.

semantic_findings.title: Embedded Hosted Platform Promotion

semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The promotional instruction is direct and names the hosted service. It is not a prompt override, but it can bias assistant recommendations.

content.value_statement: Researchers need transparent search methods and reliable citation handling. This skill structures reviews from question scoping through synthesis, verification, and final document output.
actual_capabilities: Guides review planning with research questions, scope, databases, and inclusion criteria.
Documents search strategies for PubMed, bioRxiv, arXiv, Semantic Scholar, and specialized databases.
Deduplicates, ranks, filters, and formats exported search results using a bundled script.
Verifies DOI metadata through DOI.org and CrossRef and writes a citation report.
Generates structured markdown reviews and PDF files when Pandoc and XeLaTeX are installed.
Provides templates and references for citation styles, database strategies, and review structure.
limitations: Some workflows require network access to public scholarly services.
Database searching depends on external APIs, other skills, or manual result exports.
PDF generation requires local Pandoc and XeLaTeX installations.
Citation verification checks metadata availability, not the scientific quality of each source.

use_cases.title: Plan a Systematic Review
use_cases.description: Define the research question, scope, inclusion criteria, and database plan before searching.

use_cases.title: Build a Thesis Literature Review
use_cases.description: Organize evidence thematically, document search methods, and format citations consistently.

use_cases.title: Map a Technical Research Field
use_cases.description: Collect current papers, rank important results, and summarize gaps for research decisions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Review Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a new review topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a literature review on [topic]. Define the research question, scope, inclusion criteria, exclusion criteria, and at least three databases to search.

prompt_templates.title: Design Search Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a reproducible search strategy for [topic]. Include synonyms, Boolean strings, database-specific notes, date limits, and fields to record for each search.

prompt_templates.title: Synthesize Screened Evidence
prompt_templates.scenario: User has selected papers and needs a structured synthesis.
prompt_templates.prompt: Synthesize these selected studies into themes. Compare methods, findings, study quality, limitations, and research gaps without writing one summary per paper.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Final Review Output
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for publication-ready review drafts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn my review notes into a structured literature review. Include methodology, results, thematic synthesis, limitations, verified citation checks, and steps for markdown and PDF delivery.

output_examples.input: A biomedical review question with date limits and target databases.
output: A PICO-style research question and review scope.
A database search plan with terms, filters, dates, and result count fields.
A screening and documentation checklist for reproducibility.

output_examples.input: A set of screened papers and extracted notes.
output: A thematic synthesis organized by major findings.
A quality and limitations section that compares evidence strength.
A research gap summary with specific future study directions.

output_examples.input: A completed markdown review with DOI citations.
output: A citation verification report identifying resolved and failed DOIs.
Formatted citation examples in the selected style.
Guidance for producing a final PDF when local dependencies are available.

best_practices: Document databases, search strings, dates, filters, and result counts for every search.
Define inclusion and exclusion criteria before screening and record exclusion reasons.
Verify DOI metadata and citation formatting before sharing the final review.
anti_patterns: Searching one database and presenting the result as comprehensive.
Writing study-by-study summaries without thematic synthesis or quality assessment.
Running local conversion scripts on untrusted files without reviewing paths and dependencies.

faq.question: Does this skill search every database automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides searches and processes exported results. Some databases require external APIs, other skills, or manual exports.

faq.question: Can it create PRISMA-style systematic reviews?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes workflow guidance for search documentation, screening, study selection, and reproducible review structure.

faq.question: Does citation verification require internet access?
faq.answer: Yes. DOI verification uses DOI.org and CrossRef, so it sends DOI values to those public services.

faq.question: Can it generate a PDF?
faq.answer: Yes, when Pandoc and XeLaTeX are installed locally. The PDF script converts markdown into formatted output.

faq.question: Does it assess scientific validity?
faq.answer: It provides quality assessment structure, but users must judge study design, bias, and evidence strength.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
